# EDN Core Behavioral Specification

## 1. Overview

The EDN core is the central distribution and control logic of the Entropy Distribution Network. It is responsible for forwarding CSRNG application commands, receiving entropy words from the CSRNG, and distributing that entropy to up to four endpoint interfaces as 32-bit data words.

The module shall support three high-level operating behaviors:

- Software-visible command forwarding, in which firmware writes a single CSRNG command and receives completion status.
- Auto request mode, in which the module automatically alternates between generate commands and reseed commands according to a programmed limit.
- Boot-time request mode, in which the module automatically issues a boot instantiate sequence followed by a stream of generate commands.

In all modes, entropy returned by the CSRNG shall be buffered and delivered to requesting endpoints through a request/acknowledge data interface.

## 2. Reset and Initialization

After reset, the module shall be disabled. While disabled:

- No commands shall be presented to the CSRNG.
- No endpoint shall receive an acknowledge or entropy data.
- Endpoint FIPS flags shall be cleared.
- Software command readiness shall not be asserted.
- Command queues shall be empty.
- Interrupt outputs shall be inactive.

The module shall become operational only after the enable control is set to its True value. Clearing the enable control shall cause the module to stop issuing new commands, flush command and entropy buffers, and return endpoint output interfaces to their inactive state.

The control fields shall use multi-bit encoding. The module shall ignore control values that are not valid True or False encodings and shall report such values as configuration errors. A control field with an invalid encoding shall not cause the corresponding mode to become active.

## 3. Software Command Interface

The module shall provide a software command path that allows firmware to send a single CSRNG command, such as instantiate, reseed, generate, or uninstantiate.

When the module is enabled and not in an automatic mode, it shall operate in software command mode. In this mode:

- The module shall indicate readiness to accept a new software command.
- Software shall only write a new command when readiness is indicated.
- A command written by software shall be forwarded to the CSRNG in the order it was written.
- When the CSRNG completes the command, the module shall capture the completion status and expose it to software.
- The command-done interrupt shall be asserted when a software-visible command completes and the interrupt is enabled.

While an automatic mode is active, automatically generated commands shall not update the software command status path and shall not cause the software command-done interrupt to be asserted.

The module shall also maintain command queues that can be preloaded by software for use in auto request mode. One queue is for reseed commands and one is for generate commands. Writes to the corresponding command registers shall place commands into these queues. A command FIFO reset control shall clear these queues and return them to the empty state.

## 4. Auto Request Mode

Auto request mode shall be used to produce a continuous stream of entropy without further software intervention.

Before auto request mode can operate correctly, the associated CSRNG instance must already exist. The module shall not generate an instantiate command automatically in auto request mode. Software shall first instantiate the instance through the software command path and shall load the generate and reseed command queues with the desired commands.

Auto request mode shall be active only when:

- The enable control is True.
- The auto request mode control is True.
- The boot request mode control is False.

In auto request mode, the module shall automatically issue generate commands from the generate command queue whenever entropy is needed by endpoints. The module shall track the number of generate commands issued between reseed commands. This count shall be loaded from the programmed maximum number of requests between reseeds. The count shall decrement each time a generate command is issued. When the count reaches zero, the module shall issue a reseed command from the reseed command queue before issuing further generate commands. After the reseed command completes, the count shall be reloaded from the programmed maximum.

The module shall continue this generate/reseed cycle until one of the following occurs:

- The enable control is cleared.
- The auto request mode control is cleared.
- The module is reset.

When auto request mode is exited, the module shall finish or abandon the current command sequence in a controlled manner, clear the automatic command queues, and return the software command path to its idle state.

## 5. Boot-Time Request Mode

Boot-time request mode shall provide a minimal automatic command sequence for early system boot. This mode shall take priority over auto request mode when both are configured.

Boot-time request mode shall be active when:

- The enable control is True.
- The boot request mode control is True.

In boot-time request mode, the module shall automatically take the following actions:

1. Issue an instantiate command using the preconfigured boot instantiate command value.
2. Issue the preconfigured boot generate command repeatedly to produce entropy for endpoints.
3. Continue issuing generate commands while boot-time request mode remains enabled.

Boot-time request mode shall not update software command completion status for its automatic commands. The FIPS flag associated with endpoint data in this mode shall be deasserted, because the entropy may have been produced from a pre-FIPS seed.

The module shall exit boot-time request mode when the enable control is cleared, the boot request mode control is cleared, or the module is reset. On exit, the module shall perform the shutdown sequence required to destroy the associated CSRNG instance before returning to the inactive or software-command state.

## 6. Endpoint Data Distribution

The module shall provide up to four endpoint interfaces. Each endpoint interface shall include:

- A request input.
- An acknowledge output.
- A 32-bit data bus output.
- A FIPS quality flag output.

An endpoint requests entropy by asserting its request. When a 32-bit data word is available, the module shall place the data on the endpoint data bus and assert the acknowledge signal. The endpoint consumes the word by completing the request/acknowledge handshake. After a word has been consumed, the next request shall cause the next 32-bit word to be delivered.

Entropy is received from the CSRNG in 128-bit words. The module shall make these words available to endpoints as 32-bit words. A single 128-bit word can supply up to four endpoint transfers, and those transfers may go to the same endpoint or to different endpoints.

When multiple endpoints request data at the same time, the module shall arbitrate among the requestors. Arbitration shall ensure that each pending endpoint request is eventually serviced and that no requestor is starved indefinitely.

If an endpoint requests data before any entropy is available, the module shall not acknowledge the request until data becomes available. If no endpoint is requesting data, the module shall hold the most recently received entropy data until an endpoint is ready. If internal storage is full and no endpoint is consuming data, the module shall stop accepting further entropy from the CSRNG, applying backpressure as needed.

The module shall deliver each 32-bit word only once. The data bus shall remain stable after a transfer until the next word is delivered, allowing endpoints to capture the data asynchronously.

## 7. FIPS Signaling

The module shall provide a FIPS flag on each endpoint interface to indicate whether the delivered entropy is considered FIPS-approved.

The FIPS flag shall reflect the FIPS status of the entropy word received from the CSRNG. If the CSRNG indicates that the current entropy is FIPS-compliant, the corresponding endpoint flag shall be set when that data is delivered. If the entropy is not FIPS-compliant, the flag shall be cleared.

The FIPS flag shall be cleared whenever the endpoint data path is reset or disabled. In boot-time request mode, the flag shall remain deasserted.

## 8. Entropy Integrity Checking

The module shall perform a consistency check on the entropy data received from the CSRNG. The purpose of this check is to detect repeated entropy words that could indicate a data-path fault or tampering.

The module shall compare the lower 64 bits of each consecutive 128-bit entropy word. If two consecutive words have the same lower 64-bit value, the module shall:

- Set a recoverable error status.
- Assert the recoverable alert output.

This check shall be active while the entropy data path is enabled.

## 9. Error Detection and Reporting

The module shall detect and report the following classes of errors:

- Command queue write errors, such as a write attempted when a command queue is already full.
- Command queue read errors, such as a read attempted when a command queue is empty.
- Command queue state errors, such as a queue reporting full and empty at the same time.
- Main command state machine errors.
- Endpoint acknowledge state machine errors.
- Counter errors in the request-counting logic.

All such errors shall be treated as fatal errors. When a fatal error is detected, the module shall:

- Record the error source in the error code status.
- Assert the fatal error interrupt.
- Assert the fatal alert.

The module shall also detect and report recoverable errors, including invalid control field encodings and repeated entropy data. Recoverable errors shall be recorded in the recoverable alert status and shall cause the recoverable alert output to be asserted where applicable.

Fatal error sources shall be reported regardless of whether the module is in an active operating mode. Control field configuration errors and entropy consistency errors shall be reported when their associated functions are expected to be active.

## 10. Interrupts

The module shall provide two interrupt outputs:

- Command done interrupt.
- Fatal error interrupt.

The command done interrupt shall be asserted when a software-visible command completes and the interrupt is enabled. It shall not be asserted for automatic commands generated by auto request mode or boot-time request mode.

The fatal error interrupt shall be asserted when any fatal error occurs and the interrupt is enabled.

Both interrupts shall have standard enable, status, and test controls so that software can mask, observe, and verify interrupt behavior.

## 11. Operational Status and Debug

The module shall provide software-visible status information for the current operating state. This shall include:

- A readable main state value that indicates the current high-level command state.
- Command readiness and completion status for the software command path.
- Error status for fatal and recoverable events.

These statuses shall allow firmware to determine when an automatic mode has fully shut down and when it is safe to reconfigure the module for a different mode.
